title: If you've lost your creative genius, watch this

sentences.en: Over the past few weeks, I've just felt completely brain fried and this just happens.
sentences.zh: 过去几周，我感觉脑子完全烧焦了，这种事就是会发生。

sentences.en: It feels like it happens in cycles for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它好像是周期性的。

sentences.en: Like once a year I go through this period where things just pile up the stressors, the business fires, all these other things, and I just feel off and I'm sure you know that exact feeling.
sentences.zh: 大概每年都会经历一次，各种压力、生意上的麻烦、乱七八糟的事全堆在一起，整个人就是不对劲，我敢肯定你知道那种感觉。

sentences.en: It's like you feel like you're thinking about everything and nothing at the same time, at any time of the day.
sentences.zh: 就好像一天中的任何时候，你既在思考所有事，又什么都没在想。

sentences.en: And when you try to have a good idea or you try to think deeper about something, or you try to brainstorm, just nothing's there, nothing comes to mind.
sentences.zh: 当你试图想出一个好点子，或者想深入思考某件事，或者想头脑风暴一下，脑子里就是一片空白，什么都冒不出来。

sentences.en: And it's not like a normal burnout where you're just emotionally fried.
sentences.zh: 这不像普通的倦怠，那种只是情绪上被榨干了。

sentences.en: It's just cognitive, like you can't think, you can't generate ideas.
sentences.zh: 这是认知层面的，你没法思考，没法产生想法。

sentences.en: And as a creative person, as a creator, that's the worst thing that can happen.
sentences.zh: 作为一个有创造力的人，一个创作者，这是最糟糕的事。

sentences.en: Because then, like your entire work suffers the same thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那样一来，你的整个工作都会跟着遭殃。

sentences.en: If you're starting a business or you're running a business like you need, your most valuable asset is your ability to think that is your most valuable asset is the ability to be creative, which is what this video's about.
sentences.zh: 如果你在创业或者经营一家公司，你最宝贵的资产就是你的思考能力，你最宝贵的资产就是创造的能力，这就是本期视频要讲的内容。

sentences.en: And it just feels terrible because just a month ago, writing a newsletter or an article was a breeze for me.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉太糟了，因为就在一个月前，写一封 newsletter 或一篇文章对我来说轻而易举。

sentences.en: Putting out YouTube videos, putting out content, just ideas were flowing in my brain, and that's arguably one of the best feelings for me at least.
sentences.zh: 发布 YouTube 视频、产出内容，各种想法在脑子里流动，这至少对我来说，是最好的感觉之一。

sentences.en: And the longer this went on, the feeling just compounded more.
sentences.zh: 这种状态持续得越久，那种感觉就越积越深。

sentences.en: I couldn't stop thinking like, why can't I write?
sentences.zh: 我忍不住一直想，为什么我写不出来？

sentences.en: Why can't I have good ideas?
sentences.zh: 为什么我想不出好点子？

sentences.en: I have all of these ideas that I can work with, but why can't I remember them? Why can't I think of them?
sentences.zh: 我手头明明有这么多可以用的想法，但为什么我就是记不起来？为什么我就是想不到它们？

sentences.en: And then the final question that you just get to is, how do I get that back?
sentences.zh: 然后你最终会问出那个终极问题：我怎么才能找回那种状态？

sentences.en: How do I get that creative ability back in my head?
sentences.zh: 我怎么才能把那种创造能力重新装回脑子里？

sentences.en: And that's my primary goal with this video, I want to provide a guide for both you and myself.
sentences.zh: 这就是我做这期视频的首要目标，我想为你，也为我自己，提供一份指南。

sentences.en: I'm creating this more for myself than I am for you to help us return to our most creative state, and that's very important, as you'll find my secondary goal is to show you that even if you think you aren't a creative person, you can tap into this incredibly enjoyable state of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 我做这个视频，更多是为了我自己，而不是为了你，来帮助我们回到最具创造力的状态，这非常重要，你之后会明白的。我的第二个目标是向你展示，即使你认为自己不是一个有创造力的人，你也可以进入这种极其愉悦的意识状态。

sentences.en: It's similar to the flow state, but it's potentially more potent.
sentences.zh: 它类似于心流状态，但可能更强烈。

sentences.en: You weren't focused on breezing through a set of tasks.
sentences.zh: 你不是在专注于流畅地完成一系列任务。

sentences.en: You're more so noticing things for the first time.
sentences.zh: 你更像是在第一次注意到某些事物。

sentences.en: You're seeing a deeper layer of reality that you either forgot was there or you didn't know was there in the first place.
sentences.zh: 你看到了现实更深的一层，这一层你要么忘了它存在，要么一开始就不知道它存在。

sentences.en: And it's like a dog who sees grass for the first time and they're just sniffing around and they're like, what is going on there? Dopamine is going crazy.
sentences.zh: 就像一只第一次见到草坪的狗，到处嗅来嗅去，好像在说，这里发生了什么？多巴胺在疯狂分泌。

sentences.en: And then my tertiary goal in the last section is to provide you with a seven day protocol that you can return to whenever you feel this way, so that when you go through the protocol, you hopefully go from feeling brain fried to feeling alive again.
sentences.zh: 然后我的第三个目标，在最后一部分，是给你提供一个为期七天的方案，每当你感觉不对劲的时候都可以回来用，这样当你完成这个方案后，就有望从大脑烧焦的状态，重新变得充满活力。

sentences.en: And it's a very simple protocol.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常简单的方案。

sentences.en: Many people may scoff at it and think that it's too simple, and then they'll close their minds off to it, which is the opposite of what we're trying to accomplish here.
sentences.zh: 很多人可能会嗤之以鼻，觉得它太简单了，然后关上心门，而这恰恰和我们想要达成的目标背道而驰。

sentences.en: We're trying to accomplish this open state creativity, not narrow state stressed focus.
sentences.zh: 我们想要达成的是这种开放的、有创造力的状态，而不是狭隘的、充满压力的专注。

sentences.en: And while I say it's simple, it's actually incredibly difficult to do because you've accumulated these habits over time that are keeping you in this state, right?
sentences.zh: 虽然我说它简单，但做起来其实极其困难，因为你日积月累养成的那些习惯，正把你困在这种状态里，对吧？

sentences.en: Your state of consciousness is a reflection of your behavior over time.
sentences.zh: 你的意识状态，是你长期行为的反映。

sentences.en: And so we need to undo that which can be painful.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要解除这些习惯，这个过程可能会很痛苦。

sentences.en: Now, the last reason that I'm creating this is because in today's world, your creativity is the most scarce resource.
sentences.zh: 我做这期视频的最后一个原因是，在当今世界，你的创造力是最稀缺的资源。

sentences.en: Anyone can build anything today.
sentences.zh: 今天，任何人都能构建任何东西。

sentences.en: Anyone can think anything.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以思考任何事。

sentences.en: Anyone can write anything.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以写出任何东西。

sentences.en: The people who will win in business, writing, art and just general quality of life, as always, will be those who can take the most creative path, the path that nobody else considered to take.
sentences.zh: 在商业、写作、艺术乃至整体生活质量上胜出的人，一如既往，会是那些能走最创造性路径的人——那条没人想过要去走的路。

sentences.en: So that leads to point number one, is that you don't have ideas because there's too much interference.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了第一点：你没有想法，是因为干扰太多。

sentences.en: Now, it kind of pisses me off when people say, I'm not a creative person.
sentences.zh: 说实话，当有人说“我不是个有创造力的人”时，我挺恼火的。

sentences.en: I used to say that myself, because that statement that people don't actually take the time to think through before stating it, makes creativity seem like it's just talent or skill.
sentences.zh: 我以前也这么说自己，因为这句话——人们在说出口之前根本没花时间想清楚——让创造力看起来像是天赋或技能。

sentences.en: In short, it is those things in a way, because that's what we're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，它确实是这些东西，在某种意义上，因为这就是我们在这里要谈的。

sentences.en: We're talking about how to refine the skill of creativity by getting back to your creative state.
sentences.zh: 我们要谈的是如何通过回到你的创造状态，来打磨创造力这项技能。

sentences.en: It's a skill to be able to sustain a creative state over an extended period of time.
sentences.zh: 能够长时间维持创造状态，本身就是一项技能。

sentences.en: So if you aren't in that creative state or you aren't a creative person, so to say, then you just haven't practiced the skill of getting back to that state.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你不在那个创造状态里，或者说你“不是个有创造力的人”，那你只是还没练习回到那个状态的技能。

sentences.en: Because at its core, creativity is just a natural way of being.
sentences.zh: 因为本质上，创造力就是一种自然的存在方式。

sentences.en: It's a state of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 它是一种意识状态。

sentences.en: It's a capacity that everyone has.
sentences.zh: 是每个人都具备的能力。

sentences.en: But that capacity gets buried over time.
sentences.zh: 但这种能力会随着时间被掩埋。

sentences.en: And how does it get buried?
sentences.zh: 它是怎么被掩埋的？

sentences.en: It gets buried with anything that narrows your mind because creativity is a very open, relaxed state where you see connections, patterns and possibilities that aren't immediately obvious.
sentences.zh: 被任何窄化你心智的东西掩埋，因为创造力是一种非常开放、放松的状态，你能看到那些并非显而易见的连接、模式和可能性。

sentences.en: It's the act of noticing the unnoticed, which is not the same as what most think creativity is.
sentences.zh: 它是觉察未被觉察之物的行为，这和大多数人以为的创造力不是一回事。

sentences.en: And they think that it's creating something from nothing.
sentences.zh: 他们以为那是无中生有。

sentences.en: That nothing is already there.
sentences.zh: 那个“无”其实已经在那里了。

sentences.en: It's already raw material you're creating with what's in reality.
sentences.zh: 它已经是原材料，你在用现实中已有的东西进行创造。

sentences.en: And that's a lot of stuff now, in my eyes, there are three narrow words of the mind we'll call these the three narrow or narrow words of the mind.
sentences.zh: 而现在，在我看来，心智有三种窄化，我们称之为心智的三种窄化。

sentences.en: That one's difficult, but that's what we're calling it.
sentences.zh: 这个词有点拗口，但我们就这么叫它。

sentences.en: The first is just conditioning.
sentences.zh: 第一种就是条件化。

sentences.en: Conditioning is the enemy of wonder, because when you think of creativity, you think of children, you think of your younger self because children see the world through such fresh eyes.
sentences.zh: 条件化是好奇心的敌人，因为当你想到创造力，你会想到孩子，想到小时候的自己，因为孩子用如此新鲜的眼睛看世界。

sentences.en: They haven't received the negative feedback yet from their parents or teachers or peers.
sentences.zh: 他们还没有从父母、老师或同龄人那里接收到负面反馈。

sentences.en: If a kid were to ask ChatGPT to build a teleportation device so that them in their friends can go to Pluto, nobody would bat an eye.
sentences.zh: 如果一个小孩让 ChatGPT 造一个瞬间传送装置，好让他和朋友们去冥王星，没人会觉得有什么不对。

sentences.en: They'd just be like, oh, you're so silly.
sentences.zh: 他们只会说，哦，你真傻。

sentences.en: But if you did that, they think you're an idiot.
sentences.zh: 但如果你这么做，他们会觉得你是个白痴。

sentences.en: And they just tell you that's not how the world works.
sentences.zh: 他们会直接告诉你，世界不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: You need to be more mature.
sentences.zh: 你需要更成熟一点。

sentences.en: And now I'm not saying that that's possible, but receiving negative feedback for thinking about imaginary things or creative things is the point here.
sentences.zh: 我不是说那件事是可能的，但这里的重点是：因为思考想象性的事物或创造性的事物而收到负面反馈。

sentences.en: And so the typical feedback that people receive is just guidance down the default path.
sentences.zh: 所以人们收到的典型反馈，就是被引导走向默认路径。

sentences.en: And if you stray from the default path that was created during industrialization and past generations, then you're scolded.
sentences.zh: 如果你偏离了那条在工业化和过去几代人中形成的默认路径，你就会挨骂。

sentences.en: I mean, you go to school and you receive grades so that you correct your behavior to fit into society.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你去上学，拿到分数，就是为了纠正你的行为，好让你融入社会。

sentences.en: More like the entire system is just meant to keep you on this one path, turning everyone into the same person.
sentences.zh: 更准确地说，整个系统就是要把你困在同一条路上，把所有人都变成同一个人。

sentences.en: You must go to school.
sentences.zh: 你必须上学。

sentences.en: You must do your best to get a high paying job.
sentences.zh: 你必须拼命找一份高薪工作。

sentences.en: You must praise this God, and if you disobey, you're going to hell.
sentences.zh: 你必须赞美这个神，如果你不服从，就会下地狱。

sentences.en: And if you don't get a high paying job, then you aren't respected by society.
sentences.zh: 如果你找不到高薪工作，社会就不会尊重你。

sentences.en: So by the time most people turn 20 years old, they're the exact same as everyone else.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人到20岁的时候，已经和其他人一模一样了。

sentences.en: The same thoughts, the same beliefs, the same actions.
sentences.zh: 同样的想法，同样的信念，同样的行为。

sentences.en: They're just going down the life path that was assigned to them, not the one they chose or created.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在走那条被分配给他们的人生道路，而不是自己选择或创造的那条。

sentences.en: Creativity requires holding beliefs loosely and entertaining an idea without immediately rejecting or demonizing it, as everyone does on social media, because it drives engagement and facilitates groupthink.
sentences.zh: 创造力要求你松散地持有信念，愿意接纳一个想法，而不是立刻拒绝或妖魔化它——就像社交媒体上所有人做的那样，因为那样能驱动互动，也助长了群体思维。

sentences.en: Now, the second, narrower of the mind is productivity as a priority.
sentences.zh: 第二个让心智变窄的东西，是把生产力当成第一优先级。

sentences.en: And that is a losing game because when the 9 to 5 job, the concept of the 9 to 5 job became a thing just a few hundred years ago during industrialization, 9 to 5 jobs haven't been around that long before.
sentences.zh: 那是一场必输的游戏，因为朝九晚五的工作，这个概念是几百年前工业化时期才出现的，在那之前并没有存在多久。

sentences.en: People directed their own work.
sentences.zh: 人们自己主导自己的工作。

sentences.en: They were artisans, farmers, apprentices, things of that nature.
sentences.zh: 他们是工匠、农民、学徒，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But when the 9 to 5 job became a thing, productivity became the highest value.
sentences.zh: 但当朝九晚五的工作出现后，生产力就成了最高价值。

sentences.en: It became God.
sentences.zh: 它变成了神。

sentences.en: And then everyone became a specialist in a factory that knew one piece of the puzzle.
sentences.zh: 然后每个人都成了工厂里的专家，只懂拼图的一小块。

sentences.en: They knew how to place one piece into the puzzle, because if they understood how to create the entire image themselves, they would be an entrepreneur, not an employee.
sentences.zh: 他们只知道怎么把那一块放进拼图里，因为如果他们懂得如何自己创造整幅图景，他们就会成为创业者，而不是雇员。

sentences.en: The trap that I fall into and you probably fall into and everyone falls into, is that they just feel like they're falling behind.
sentences.zh: 我掉进去的陷阱，你大概也掉进去的陷阱，每个人都掉进去的陷阱，就是总觉得自己落后了。

sentences.en: I mean, have you seen Claude on Twitter? Anthropic.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你看到 Claude 在 Twitter 上吗？Anthropic 那个。

sentences.en: Just pushing out updates.
sentences.zh: 不停地在推更新。

sentences.en: It just feels like we're in this speed tunnel or something that feels like you just can't keep up.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像我们被困在一个速度隧道里，你根本跟不上。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm building a software and we made the mistake of competing with AI companies in general, and we just feel like we constantly have to keep up.
sentences.zh: 我正在做一个软件，我们犯了一个错误，就是试图跟 AI 公司竞争，结果就是总觉得自己必须不断追赶。

sentences.en: And so we're taking a step back and looking at what's going to be here no matter what.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在退一步，去看那些无论如何都会存在的东西。

sentences.en: What are the human things that we need to help facilitate, like creativity, so that we aren't just constantly stuck in this hype cycle?
sentences.zh: 那些我们需要帮助促成的人类特质是什么，比如创造力，这样我们才不会永远困在这个炒作循环里。

sentences.en: And even if you're not building a company, you just feel like you're behind.
sentences.zh: 就算你不是在创业，你也会觉得自己落后了。

sentences.en: And if you're being real, you're never going to catch up.
sentences.zh: 说实话，你永远也追不上。

sentences.en: You're always going to feel that way.
sentences.zh: 你永远都会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: So what's the only way out? Creativity.
sentences.zh: 那唯一的出路是什么？创造力。

sentences.en: And the thing with always feeling behind is that there's always this deadline.
sentences.zh: 而总是感觉落后的关键在于，永远有一个截止日期。

sentences.en: There's always some kind of deadline there.
sentences.zh: 那里永远有某种截止日期。

sentences.en: And if you know what that deadline does, it's very good for productivity.
sentences.zh: 如果你知道那个截止日期的作用，它对生产力非常有效。

sentences.en: It's a productivity hack if you choose it, if you implement it yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果你自己选择它、自己实施它，它是一个生产力技巧。

sentences.en: But if there's just this invisible deadline in your life all the time, that just leads to a constantly stressed and narrowed mind.
sentences.zh: 但如果你的生活中一直有一个无形的截止日期，那只会导致一个持续紧张、持续变窄的心智。

sentences.en: And that's just the thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: If your life isn't centered around efficiency and optimization in today's world, everyone just thinks you're useless because that's the normal way to live.
sentences.zh: 在今天这个时代，如果你的生活不以效率和优化为中心，所有人都会觉得你没用，因为那才是"正常"的活法。

sentences.en: In other words, if you aren't a robot, you're useless.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你不是一台机器，你就是没用的。

sentences.en: But that's exactly what creativity demands.
sentences.zh: 但这恰恰是创造力所需要的。

sentences.en: It demands useless wandering through boredom or creating space for the right idea to emerge.
sentences.zh: 它需要你在无聊中漫无目的地游荡，或者为那个正确的想法留出浮现的空间。

sentences.en: That will take you much further than the productivity bro stuck in the same race as everyone else.
sentences.zh: 这会让你走得更远，远超那些跟所有人挤在同一条赛道上的"生产力达人"。

sentences.en: People who schedule every hour of their day don't stumble onto anything.
sentences.zh: 把每一天每个小时都排满的人，永远不会偶然撞见什么。

sentences.en: Now.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: The third narrower of the mind is having infinite input with zero processing time.
sentences.zh: 第三个让思维变窄的原因，是无限输入却零处理时间。

sentences.en: So I want you to think about fitness or health.
sentences.zh: 我想让你想想健身或者健康这件事。

sentences.en: It's kind of obvious that your metabolism can only go so fast, and if you're in niche circles on social media, there's always this group that's just trying to speed up their metabolism, speed up their metabolism, and I guess they get it to work to some extent.
sentences.zh: 很明显，你的新陈代谢速度是有上限的。如果你在社交媒体上混某些小众圈子，总有一群人整天想着加速新陈代谢、加速新陈代谢，我猜他们多少也搞出了一些效果。

sentences.en: But there's a limit.
sentences.zh: 但总有个极限。

sentences.en: Like you weren't just going to burn 10,000 calories a day without running or doing cardio for that amount of time, and then you're just going to drive yourself into the ground.
sentences.zh: 你不可能一天烧掉一万大卡，却不跑那么长时间、不做那么长时间的有氧，然后你只会把自己榨干。

sentences.en: Why would you even do that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要那么做？

sentences.en: Nobody even wants to eat that much food, but it's obvious that you have a certain level of metabolism, how much you can burn in a day, and if you eat over that, if you overeat food, then you get fat.
sentences.zh: 根本没人想吃那么多东西。但很明显，你有一个固定的新陈代谢水平，一天能消耗多少是有限的。如果你吃超了，吃太多了，你就会变胖。

sentences.en: Of course, this is over an extended period of time, but most people don't realize that this applies to the mind as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是长期累积的结果。但大多数人没有意识到，这个道理同样适用于大脑。

sentences.en: You have a set amount of information that you can digest and metabolize and actually use, and that's the problem.
sentences.zh: 你能消化、代谢并真正使用的信息量是有限的，而这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: People feel like they always have to keep up, so they feel like if they don't listen to ten podcasts a week that they won't be able to keep up, they'll be useless.
sentences.zh: 人们总觉得必须跟上一切，觉得如果一周不听十个播客，就会跟不上，就会变得没用。

sentences.en: And now there's a time for consuming information or researching information, a curated set of information that helps spark more ideas.
sentences.zh: 当然，确实有需要消费信息或研究信息的时候，一套精心筛选的信息能帮你激发更多想法。

sentences.en: But if it isn't kept under tight control, then you overeat. You over consume.
sentences.zh: 但如果不好好控制，你就会吃撑。你会过度消费。

sentences.en: Now I write content, I write newsletters, I write tweets.
sentences.zh: 我写内容，写 newsletter，写推文。

sentences.en: That's like my foundation, I love writing, that's it.
sentences.zh: 那是我的根基，我热爱写作，仅此而已。

sentences.en: If I don't write in the morning, my day kind of sucks.
sentences.zh: 如果我早上不写点东西，那一天就感觉不太对劲。

sentences.en: And I know that I shouldn't bank everything.
sentences.zh: 我知道我不该把一切

sentences.en: On being able to write good ideas in the morning, but that's just kind of how it is. I really like writing.
sentences.zh: 都押在早上能不能写出好点子上，但事实就是这样，我真的很喜欢写作。

sentences.en: I love the process of capturing ideas, internalizing them, thinking about them, researching them, strengthening them stress testing them, and then putting them out into the world to see if they help people, and then getting feedback.
sentences.zh: 我热爱这个过程：捕捉想法、内化它们、思考它们、研究它们、强化它们、对它们进行压力测试，然后把它们放到世界上，看看能不能帮到别人，再获得反馈。

sentences.en: So it refines it further.
sentences.zh: 这样就能进一步打磨它。

sentences.en: I mean, in today's world, like, isn't that just incredible that you can talk about your interests and other people can find it interesting?
sentences.zh: 说真的，在今天这个时代，你能聊自己感兴趣的东西，而别人也会觉得有趣，这难道不不可思议吗？

sentences.en: And then if you do the right things, you can turn that into a source of income.
sentences.zh: 然后如果你做了正确的事，你还能把它变成收入来源。

sentences.en: It's pretty freaking cool, if you ask me.
sentences.zh: 要我说，这真的挺酷的。

sentences.en: But with that, the way I used to think is that I need to consume information in order to have ideas so that I can put out into the world.
sentences.zh: 但说到这个，我以前的想法是，我必须消费信息才能有想法，才能把东西输出到世界上。

sentences.en: So if I struggle to write or to have ideas, I felt like I just wasn't consuming good information, which is kind of true, but creativity is rarely an input problem.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我写不出来，或者没有想法，我就觉得是自己没消费到好的信息。这有一定道理，但创造力很少是输入的问题。

sentences.en: I love the saying that you can only cook with what's in the fridge, but most people's fridges are just overflowing with like, candy and ice cream and trash.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢一句话：你只能用冰箱里现有的食材做饭。但大多数人的冰箱里塞满了糖果、冰淇淋和垃圾。

sentences.en: Now, as an aside, I'm doing a writing challenge that probably starts in a little over one week.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一句，我正在做一个写作挑战，大概一周多后开始。

sentences.en: By the time this video goes out, it's going to be called build a two hour Content System.
sentences.zh: 等这个视频发出来的时候，它应该叫"构建一个两小时内容系统"。

sentences.en: In 14 days, it's 14 days long.
sentences.zh: 14 天，整个挑战为期 14 天。

sentences.en: You get 14 AI prompts, so one every day.
sentences.zh: 你会拿到 14 个 AI 提示词，每天一个。

sentences.en: And these aren't I prompts that write posts for you or write newsletters for you.
sentences.zh: 而且这些不是那种替你写帖子、替你写 newsletter 的提示词。

sentences.en: We're not that desperate yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还没绝望到那个地步。

sentences.en: They help refine your thinking.
sentences.zh: 它们是帮你打磨思考的。

sentences.en: They help stress test ideas. They help you learn.
sentences.zh: 帮你对想法做压力测试。帮你学习。

sentences.en: They help you gain clarity on what you actually want to do, what you actually want to write about.
sentences.zh: 帮你搞清楚你到底想做什么、到底想写什么。

sentences.en: They help you learn how to structure your ideas in a way that captures attention and becomes more valuable, so that you don't just put out fortune cookie tweets and act like your Marcus Aurelius when nobody's going to care about you because you're not Marcus Aurelius.
sentences.zh: 帮你学会如何组织想法，让它们能抓住注意力、变得更有价值，这样你就不会只是发一些鸡汤推文，然后装得跟 Marcus Aurelius 似的——没人会在乎你，因为你不是 Marcus Aurelius。

sentences.en: The reason I'm running this is because I just need that intensive challenge.
sentences.zh: 我做这个挑战的原因很简单，我就是需要那种高强度训练。

sentences.en: I'm going to be doing it with you, and it's meant to get your creative juices flowing.
sentences.zh: 我会跟你一起做，目的就是让你的创造力流动起来。

sentences.en: And you'll also understand why I'm creating this in the very last section of this video.
sentences.zh: 而且你会在视频最后一部分明白我为什么要做这个。

sentences.en: Because in order to be creative, you need something to create.
sentences.zh: 因为要想有创造力，你得先有东西可创造。

sentences.en: So by the end of the challenge, you'll have some kind of brand, an understanding of what your unique voice is, a batch of nonstop social posts, and the first draft, or even the first polished piece of a newsletter article, Substack, whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以挑战结束时，你会拥有某种品牌雏形、对自己独特声音的理解、一批不间断的社交帖子，以及一篇 newsletter 文章或 Substack 之类的初稿，甚至可能是第一篇打磨好的成品。

sentences.en: And since ex articles are doing really well right now, and articles longform writing is a moat in today's world because I can't really replicate it.
sentences.zh: 而且现在 X 上的文章表现非常好，长文写作在当今世界是一条护城河，因为我没法真正复制它。

sentences.en: It's never been a better time to start writing, especially authentically.
sentences.zh: 现在开始写作是最好的时机，尤其是真诚地写。

sentences.en: So I would join before the challenge starts using the link in the description, and I hope to see you in there.
sentences.zh: 所以趁挑战还没开始，用描述里的链接加入，希望能在里面见到你。

sentences.en: Now, point number two, you're not bored, you're overstimulated.
sentences.zh: 好，第二点：你不是无聊，你是过度刺激了。

sentences.en: And now I say this because boredom is how you really tap into creativity in a creative state.
sentences.zh: 我说这个是因为，无聊才是你真正进入创造状态、触及创造力的方式。

sentences.en: It's how you get ideas to just pop into your head.
sentences.zh: 想法就是这样突然冒进你脑子里的。

sentences.en: But then people say that they're bored all the time and they're not creative.
sentences.zh: 但人们总说自己一直很无聊，却没什么创造力。

sentences.en: And that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这。

sentences.en: Being chronically overcaffeinated and overstimulated is not boredom.
sentences.zh: 长期咖啡因过量、刺激过量，那不叫无聊。

sentences.en: You're so fried mentally that you've gone all the way off the deep end, and then you associate that with boredom, because things that would previously give you euphoria or enjoyment don't even impact you anymore.
sentences.zh: 你精神上已经彻底枯竭了，走到了崩溃的尽头，然后你把这种感觉跟无聊混为一谈，因为以前能让你兴奋或享受的东西，现在对你已经毫无影响了。

sentences.en: So you just you're bored all the time because literally nothing can excite you.
sentences.zh: 所以你一直觉得无聊，因为真的没有任何东西能让你兴奋起来。

sentences.en: And so you quite literally can't go any further away from true boredom.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你离真正的无聊已经远到不能再远了。

sentences.en: You have to go back.
sentences.zh: 你得往回走。

sentences.en: And so true boredom, after you go through your withdrawal period does a few things.
sentences.zh: 而真正的无聊，在你熬过戒断期之后，会做几件事。

sentences.en: First is that boredom is a gateway into novelty novel ideas, new things.
sentences.zh: 首先，无聊是通往新奇想法、新事物的入口。

sentences.en: So many of you know Carl Jung OG psychologist, but he harped on the importance of shadow work, which is confronting the uncomfortable aspects of ourselves that we typically avoid.
sentences.zh: 你们很多人知道 Carl Jung，那位 OG 心理学家，他反复强调阴影工作的重要性，也就是直面我们通常回避的、自己身上不舒服的部分。

sentences.en: And sitting with boredom does just this.
sentences.zh: 而跟无聊共处，做的正是这件事。

sentences.en: It activates breakthrough insights when the rational mind stops trying to solve everything.
sentences.zh: 当理性思维停止试图解决一切时，它会激活突破性的洞见。

sentences.en: And an important thing here, whether you're trying to be creative or just trying to get out of a rut, is that true?
sentences.zh: 这里有一个关键点，不管你是想变得有创造力，还是只想走出困境——这是真的。

sentences.en: Boredom sets the scene for three flow triggers, and what I mean by that is you're more likely to enter this intense period of flow like this monk mode, so to say, where you're just making progress nonstop.
sentences.zh: 无聊为三种心流触发器搭建了舞台，我的意思是，你更有可能进入那种高强度的、像闭关模式一样的心流状态，就是那种你不停取得进展的状态。

sentences.en: Because in order to do that, you do need a creative idea.
sentences.zh: 因为要做到这一点，你确实需要一个创造性的想法。

sentences.en: You need this influx.
sentences.zh: 你需要这种涌入。

sentences.en: You need good ideas, idea flow because you need to you need something to build.
sentences.zh: 你需要好点子、创意流，因为你需要有东西可建。

sentences.en: So those three flow triggers are one deep embodiment, which is just being present with discomfort to novelty because boredom forces you to seek new, healthier stimulation.
sentences.zh: 所以那三个心流触发器是：一，深度具身，也就是带着不适感去面对新奇，因为无聊会逼你寻找新的、更健康的刺激。

sentences.en: And three unpredictability, which is not knowing what will emerge from the void.
sentences.zh: 三，不可预测性，也就是你不知道虚空里会冒出什么。

sentences.en: So if you don't know what you should do with your life, maybe you should do nothing.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不知道自己这辈子该做什么，也许你该什么都不做。

sentences.en: And I mean actually nothing.
sentences.zh: 我说的是真正的什么都不做。

sentences.en: Not the default, nothing that everyone else falls into.
sentences.zh: 不是其他人陷入的那种默认的“什么都不做”。

sentences.en: The second thing that true boredom helps facilitate is that the brain up regulates dopamine receptors when it's deprived.
sentences.zh: 真正的无聊促成的第二件事是：当大脑被剥夺刺激时，它会向上调节多巴胺受体。

sentences.en: Hedonic adaptation is your psychological thermostat.
sentences.zh: 享乐适应就是你的心理恒温器。

sentences.en: No matter how high or low the temperature goes, it always tries to return to the set point.
sentences.zh: 不管温度升得多高、降得多低，它总是试图回到那个设定点。

sentences.en: Now, this creates what psychologists call the hedonic treadmill.
sentences.zh: 这就形成了心理学家所说的享乐跑步机。

sentences.en: I'm sure you've heard of it before, where you're always running toward the next source of pleasure, but the satisfaction nevertheless, each experience becomes your new normal, requiring more intense stimulation to achieve the same emotional high.
sentences.zh: 我肯定你以前听过，你总在奔向下一个快感来源，但满足感却转瞬即逝，每一次体验都变成你的新常态，需要更强烈的刺激才能达到同样的情绪高潮。

sentences.en: But when you deprive yourself of pleasure, the opposite happens.
sentences.zh: 但当你剥夺自己的快感时，相反的事情就会发生。

sentences.en: It's a hedonic reversal.
sentences.zh: 这是一种享乐逆转。

sentences.en: So slowly, then rapidly, simple pleasures become enjoyable again.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，然后迅速地，简单的快乐重新变得令人享受。

sentences.en: And you notice this. I'm sure you've noticed it before.
sentences.zh: 你注意到了这一点。我肯定你以前注意到过。

sentences.en: You just haven't registered it as something that you can actually do in control.
sentences.zh: 你只是没意识到这是你可以主动控制的事情。

sentences.en: And when this happens, it's like you notice the detail in the sky again, or when you have a good meal, you notice that you can like pick apart the flavors.
sentences.zh: 当这发生时，就像你重新注意到天空的细节，或者当你吃到一顿好饭时，你发现你能分辨出其中的风味层次。

sentences.en: You're not just pounding down food and like, oh, this is so good.
sentences.zh: 你不再只是狼吞虎咽，然后说“哦，这太好吃了”。

sentences.en: You have a well cooked meal and you're like, oh, is that a sort of hint of rosemary?
sentences.zh: 你吃到一顿精心烹制的饭菜，你会想“哦，这是不是有一丝迷迭香的味道？”

sentences.en: You feel more sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 你感觉自己更细腻了。

sentences.en: In other words, life becomes electric as it should be.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，生活变得充满电流感，就像它本该如此。

sentences.en: Now, the third thing that boredom helps facilitate is that you don't need motivation.
sentences.zh: 无聊促成的第三件事是：你不需要动力。

sentences.en: You need clarity.
sentences.zh: 你需要的是清晰。

sentences.en: So a quote from novel to nail this nail in the coffin.
sentences.zh: 引用一句话来盖棺定论。

sentences.en: All of humanity's problems stem from man's inability to sit quietly in a room alone.
sentences.zh: 人类所有的问题都源于人无法独自安静地坐在房间里。

sentences.en: So boredom creates space for sense making, that is, processing and integrating experience.
sentences.zh: 所以无聊为意义建构创造了空间，也就是处理和整合经验。

sentences.en: So if you're consuming too much information, you just need to stop.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在消费太多信息，你只需要停下来。

sentences.en: Now on to the third section that you've been waiting for, which is the seven day protocol to slow the fuck down for those who want to feel alive again.
sentences.zh: 现在进入你一直在等的第三部分：七天放慢节奏的方案，献给那些想重新感觉自己还活着的人。

sentences.en: Because I'm sure you get it by now.
sentences.zh: 因为我肯定你现在已经明白了。

sentences.en: Creativity is important, and you should probably prioritize it more. But how?
sentences.zh: 创造力很重要，你可能应该更优先对待它。但怎么做？

sentences.en: How do you actually prioritize this thing?
sentences.zh: 你到底怎么优先对待这件事？

sentences.en: And it's the same way you get results in anything.
sentences.zh: 这跟你做任何事拿到结果的方式一样。

sentences.en: We look at the problem, which is being mentally overweight or mentally bloated or overstimulated, and then we design a system that results in the alleviation of those things.
sentences.zh: 我们看问题所在——精神超重、精神臃肿、过度刺激——然后我们设计一个系统，来缓解这些东西。

sentences.en: And true change is behavior change.
sentences.zh: 真正的改变是行为改变。

sentences.en: The only way to solve a problem for good is to change your own behavior.
sentences.zh: 彻底解决问题的唯一方法，是改变你自己的行为。

sentences.en: And so that sounds kind of obvious, but a lot of the times you don't notice your own problems.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像废话，但很多时候你根本意识不到自己的问题。

sentences.en: So that's why a video like this can be helpful, because it can shine a light of awareness on something you were blind to before.
sentences.zh: 所以这种视频才有用，它能照亮你之前看不见的盲区。

sentences.en: And sure, you can ask ChatGPT for this stuff, but you can't ask ChatGPT what you don't know to ask.
sentences.zh: 当然，你可以去问 ChatGPT，但你没法问 ChatGPT 你不知道要问什么。

sentences.en: Now, we don't need a full dopamine detox like I've talked about in a previous video, but we do need to commit.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要做我之前视频里说的那种完整的多巴胺戒断，但我们需要承诺。

sentences.en: We need to commit for one week.
sentences.zh: 我们需要承诺一周。

sentences.en: So that's my challenge to you.
sentences.zh: 这就是我给你的挑战。

sentences.en: And as I said, this is very simple.
sentences.zh: 我说了，这件事非常简单。

sentences.en: I'm going to go through it and you're being like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我讲的时候你可能会觉得，嗯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So people are going to think that they're above it.
sentences.zh: 有些人会觉得这太简单了，不值得做。

sentences.en: And that's an enemy of creativity.
sentences.zh: 这是创造力的敌人。

sentences.en: So no matter how simple you think this is, just fucking do it.
sentences.zh: 所以不管你觉得自己多厉害，直接去做就对了。

sentences.en: Because that's one reason you aren't very creative.
sentences.zh: 因为你不够有创意，这就是原因之一。

sentences.en: So days one and two tomorrow and the next day you're going to reduce input fast.
sentences.zh: 第一天和第二天，也就是明天和后天，你要快速减少输入。

sentences.en: And this is going to be the equivalent of intermittent fasting for your mind.
sentences.zh: 这相当于给你的大脑做间歇性断食。

sentences.en: We're not doing a seven day fast, but we're doing some kind of intermittent fasting, some kind of deprive.
sentences.zh: 我们不做七天断食，但要做某种间歇性断食，某种剥夺。

sentences.en: So the first thing impose strict time blocks on your work day, if you can.
sentences.zh: 第一件事：如果条件允许，给你的工作日设置严格的时间块。

sentences.en: You want to limit work to four hours a day for this next week.
sentences.zh: 接下来这一周，把工作时间限制在每天四小时。

sentences.en: And if you can't do that, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 如果做不到，也没关系。

sentences.en: Just set an alarm that marks the end of your work, and when it goes off, you're done.
sentences.zh: 就设一个闹钟标记工作结束，闹钟一响，你就收工。

sentences.en: You're not doing one last task.
sentences.zh: 不再做最后一个任务。

sentences.en: Your job is to not think about work or productivity.
sentences.zh: 你的任务是不去想工作或效率。

sentences.en: When you're not working, you're practicing the skill of letting something feel unfinished without anxiety or without the stress of feeling like you're not keeping up because you're not doing anything when you're not at work anyways.
sentences.zh: 不工作的时候，你在练习一种能力：让事情保持未完成状态，不焦虑，不觉得跟不上，因为你不在工作时本来也没做什么。

sentences.en: Second thing is to cut out your primary input source.
sentences.zh: 第二件事：切断你的主要输入源。

sentences.en: It's like the junk food in the cabinet at night.
sentences.zh: 就像晚上柜子里的垃圾食品。

sentences.en: You want to pick the one source you reach for the most mindlessly and then eliminate that.
sentences.zh: 找出你最容易无意识去刷的那一个来源，然后把它干掉。

sentences.en: So this could be the podcast on your commute.
sentences.zh: 可能是通勤路上听的播客。

sentences.en: Could be the scroll before bed or in the morning.
sentences.zh: 可能是睡前或起床时的刷手机。

sentences.en: Could also be the news in the morning.
sentences.zh: 也可能是早上的新闻。

sentences.en: If people still watch news nowadays and just replace it with nothing, sit in silence.
sentences.zh: 如果现在还有人看新闻的话。用空白来替代它，安静地坐着。

sentences.en: Listen for an idea.
sentences.zh: 倾听一个想法。

sentences.en: And the third thing as many could have guessed is to go on a walk.
sentences.zh: 第三件事，很多人可能猜到了：去散步。

sentences.en: Not because it will do anything magical for you just yet, but because ideas are caught in motion.
sentences.zh: 不是因为它马上会带来什么神奇效果，而是因为灵感是在运动中捕捉到的。

sentences.en: So don't use any headphones and even leave your phone at home if you have to.
sentences.zh: 所以别戴耳机，必要的话把手机也留在家里。

sentences.en: This walk won't do much for you yet, since it may be your first time, but just trust the process.
sentences.zh: 这次散步暂时不会给你带来太大改变，毕竟可能是你第一次这么做，但相信这个过程就好。

sentences.en: So that's it. Day one and two three simple changes.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。第一天和第二天，三个简单的改变。

sentences.en: And psychologically, removing constant input allows your brain's default mode network, which is the brain's wandering system to fire.
sentences.zh: 从心理层面来说，切断持续的信息输入，会让大脑的默认模式网络——也就是大脑的漫游系统——开始活跃。

sentences.en: This is the network responsible for random insight, self-reflection, and imagining the future.
sentences.zh: 这个网络负责随机顿悟、自我反思和想象未来。

sentences.en: It cannot be active while you're consuming.
sentences.zh: 当你在消费内容时，它是无法被激活的。

sentences.en: Now days three and four, we're going to digest the information that's already there, and we're going to practice digesting information in general.
sentences.zh: 到了第三天和第四天，我们要去消化那些已经存在的信息，并且练习消化信息这件事本身。

sentences.en: So now that you've created space, it may feel like a flood of ideas are coming in, not just ideas, but information in general.
sentences.zh: 既然你已经腾出了空间，可能会感觉大量想法涌入，不只是想法，而是各种信息。

sentences.en: It's going to feel kind of chaotic because your mind is opening up.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得有点混乱，因为你的大脑正在打开。

sentences.en: It's starting to let things in that have just been there for a long time.
sentences.zh: 它开始让那些已经存在了很久的东西浮现出来。

sentences.en: You're going to notice unfinished thoughts.
sentences.zh: 你会注意到那些未完成的思绪。

sentences.en: You might remember things.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想起一些事情。

sentences.en: You're going to notice suppressed feelings or random connections, or just ideas you forgot existed.
sentences.zh: 你会注意到被压抑的感受，或者随机的关联，或者那些你忘了它们曾经存在过的想法。

sentences.en: So during this phase, what we're going to do as we're digesting this information is we're going to try to notice the deeper layers of reality.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个阶段，当我们在消化这些信息时，我们要试着去觉察现实更深层的部分。

sentences.en: So the first thing is to read one chapter of a book slowly, like way too slowly, like you feel like you weren't doing anything because you aren't trying to finish the book, right.
sentences.zh: 第一件事，是慢慢地读一本书的一章，慢到离谱，慢到你觉得好像什么都没做，因为你本来就不是为了读完这本书。

sentences.en: You don't have the goal, the productive goal of finishing X amount of books in a year.
sentences.zh: 你没有那种目标，没有那种“一年读完多少本书”的效率目标。

sentences.en: You're not even trying to learn something.
sentences.zh: 你甚至不是在试图学什么东西。

sentences.en: You're just trying to simply notice when a sentence makes you stop and think you're not reading past it.
sentences.zh: 你只是在试着觉察，当某一句话让你停下来思考时，你就不要再往下读了。

sentences.en: When it does, you just put the book down.
sentences.zh: 当那句话出现时，你就把书放下。

sentences.en: You sit with why that line hit you.
sentences.zh: 你坐下来，体会为什么那句话击中了你。

sentences.en: You think about it in in my eyes, this is the best way to read in general.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这本来就是最好的阅读方式。

sentences.en: Like, you don't have to finish books and you don't have to try to do it quickly because you're hoping that someone will care that you finished it quickly.
sentences.zh: 你不需要把书读完，也不需要试图快速读完，因为你并不需要别人在意你读得有多快。

sentences.en: Just get what you need and put the book down.
sentences.zh: 拿到你需要的东西，然后把书放下。

sentences.en: That one idea will impact you more than the entire book if you actually think about it.
sentences.zh: 那一个想法，如果你真的去思考它，会比整本书对你的影响更大。

sentences.en: So you're going to do that once a day.
sentences.zh: 你每天做一次这件事。

sentences.en: Do it in the morning, just like start the day with something like that, because then the rest of your day will be a bit more creative.
sentences.zh: 在早上做，用这样一件事开启你的一天，因为接下来一整天你都会更有创造力。

sentences.en: Now, if you want to stack this with number two, here's what number two is.
sentences.zh: 如果你想把这个和第二件事叠加起来做，第二件事是这样的。

sentences.en: You can do this right after.
sentences.zh: 你可以在读完书之后马上做。

sentences.en: And that's sit with nothing for ten minutes.
sentences.zh: 那就是什么都不做，坐十分钟。

sentences.en: You can call it meditation, sure, but I don't want you to use a meditation app or any guided breathing technique.
sentences.zh: 你可以叫它冥想，没问题，但我不希望你用冥想 App 或任何引导式呼吸技巧。

sentences.en: Just sit somewhere and let your mind do whatever it wants.
sentences.zh: 就找个地方坐下，让你的大脑想干什么就干什么。

sentences.en: It will be chaotic at first, but that's the digestion happening.
sentences.zh: 一开始会很混乱，但那正是消化在发生。

sentences.en: Don't do anything with it, just sit.
sentences.zh: 不要对它做任何事，只是坐着。

sentences.en: And now the third thing.
sentences.zh: 然后是第三件事。

sentences.en: Keep going on a walk.
sentences.zh: 继续去散步。

sentences.en: One walk a day or two, or however many same rules, no headphones or any stimulation.
sentences.zh: 一天走一两次，或者随便多少次，规则一样：不戴耳机，不接受任何刺激。

sentences.en: But this time try to actually see things you pass by these things 100 times about.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，试着真正去看你路过的东西——这些东西你大概已经路过一百次了。

sentences.en: Have you noticed a detail in the sidewalk?
sentences.zh: 你有没有注意过人行道上的某个细节？

sentences.en: Have you noticed the structure of the trees, branches, or the vastness of the sky?
sentences.zh: 你有没有注意过树的结构、树枝的形态，或者天空的辽阔？

sentences.en: And in terms of looking at the sky, I bet you didn't even look up the last walk.
sentences.zh: 说到看天空，我敢打赌你上次散步时连头都没抬过。

sentences.en: So what we're trying to do here is release the grip that you have on your subconscious, which is the thing responsible for kind of processing background tasks and surfacing those moments.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里试图做的，是松开你对潜意识的控制——潜意识负责处理后台任务，并让那些灵光闪现的时刻浮现出来。

sentences.en: And the best way to do this is just stepping away from task oriented work.
sentences.zh: 而做到这一点的最好方式，就是从任务导向的工作中抽身离开。

sentences.en: And if those moments of insight or those moments allow you to do less but higher leveraged work, that gets more results, then aren't you being more productive by not trying to be productive?
sentences.zh: 如果那些洞察时刻、那些灵光闪现让你做得更少，但做的是杠杆更高的工作，带来更多结果，那么你通过“不试图高效”反而变得更高效了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Aren't you getting more done by not working now for day five and six?
sentences.zh: 你不工作，反而完成了更多事情，不是吗？现在进入第五天和第六天。

sentences.en: The goal or the intention is to just become interested in life again, because something I think about often when people say, oh, I just don't find anything interesting, right?
sentences.zh: 目标或者说意图，就是重新对生活产生兴趣。因为我经常想到一件事，当人们说“哦，我就是对什么都提不起兴趣”的时候——

sentences.en: When I was a kid, a certain age, like people ask, oh, what are you interested in?
sentences.zh: 当我还是小孩的时候，到了某个年纪，别人会问，哦，你对什么感兴趣？

sentences.en: And I think, well, I guess the gym, I guess this, I guess this, but no, not really anything.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，嗯，大概是健身吧，大概是这个，大概是那个，但不，其实真的没什么。

sentences.en: And now I can't help but wonder, like, haven't you looked around like I'm looking at a camera like it's so weird.
sentences.zh: 而现在我忍不住会想，难道你没环顾过四周吗？就像我现在看着一台相机，这东西太奇怪了。

sentences.en: I know it sounds stupid to think this way, but that's exactly what I talked about at the beginning of this thing.
sentences.zh: 我知道这么想听起来很蠢，但这恰恰是我在这个视频开头说的东西。

sentences.en: Like, allow yourself to romanticize things a bit, like this camera, this piece of technology is just incredible.
sentences.zh: 允许自己稍微浪漫化一些事物，比如这台相机，这件技术产品简直不可思议。

sentences.en: I don't know anything about it.
sentences.zh: 我对它一无所知。

sentences.en: I don't know how to recreate one.
sentences.zh: 我不知道怎么再造一台出来。

sentences.en: It it's a work of art.
sentences.zh: 它是一件艺术品。

sentences.en: It's a work of genius.
sentences.zh: 它是一件天才之作。

sentences.en: And it's mass produced at scale.
sentences.zh: 而且它被大规模量产。

sentences.en: And it allows me to talk to you, like, asynchronously.
sentences.zh: 它让我能和你对话，以异步的方式。

sentences.en: And if I just let my mind continue to go down that rabbit hole and don't let any beliefs or like thinking this is just an immature line of thinking, if I don't let that stop me, then I get to some kind of idea.
sentences.zh: 如果我放任自己的思绪顺着那个兔子洞一直往下走，不让任何信念、或者“这只是幼稚的思考方式”这种想法阻止我，那么我就会触达某种想法。

sentences.en: I start thinking about how it's how it was done.
sentences.zh: 我开始思考它是怎么做出来的。

sentences.en: How can I replicate that?
sentences.zh: 我怎么能复制它？

sentences.en: How can I learn about this thing?
sentences.zh: 我怎么能学会这个东西？

sentences.en: How can I apply something in this camera to my business?
sentences.zh: 我怎么能把相机里的某些东西应用到我的生意上？

sentences.en: Or even that's like going down the productive line of thinking, but just let yourself go crazy.
sentences.zh: 甚至——这已经偏向那条“高效”的思考路线了——但就让自己疯一点吧。

sentences.en: And that's the thing is, like your mind and my mind at times is just so occupied with meaningless shit that we don't think anything is interesting when all of life is interesting.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这里：你的大脑、我的大脑，有时候被太多毫无意义的垃圾占据，以至于我们觉得什么都不有趣，而实际上，生活的全部都是有趣的。

sentences.en: So by now in this protocol, the mental fog in your mind should be lifting.
sentences.zh: 所以到了这个流程的现在，你脑中的精神迷雾应该正在消散。

sentences.en: You feel a bit sharper and the colors are a bit more vivid.
sentences.zh: 你感觉思维更敏锐了一点，色彩更鲜活了一点。

sentences.en: If you actually try to notice them and small things feel meaningful again, you walk outside and you just finally, like, enjoy a breath of fresh air.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的试着去注意它们的话——小事情重新变得有意义了。你走到外面，终于，真正享受了一口新鲜空气。

sentences.en: When was the last time you enjoyed a breath of fresh air?
sentences.zh: 你上一次享受一口新鲜空气是什么时候？

sentences.en: So three things for these days five and six.
sentences.zh: 所以第五天和第六天，有三件事。

sentences.en: First, trust that ideas will come back.
sentences.zh: 第一，相信灵感会回来。

sentences.en: What I mean is that you should resist the urge to take notes on everything.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你要克制住什么都记下来的冲动。

sentences.en: If it's important, it will find its way back to you.
sentences.zh: 如果它真的重要，它会自己找回来的。

sentences.en: When I'm talking with my co-founders on this, when we're building a software in order to capture ideas or to have ideas, I often think about this when I jot down ideas like if they're more than seven days old, I'm not going to go back to them.
sentences.zh: 我跟我的联合创始人聊这个的时候，我们在做一款捕捉想法、激发想法的软件，我经常想到这一点：我记下的想法，如果超过七天我都没回头去看——

sentences.en: Like I'm not going to remember them.
sentences.zh: 那我也不会再想起来了。

sentences.en: And if it's important, it will find its way back to the top of my notes.
sentences.zh: 而如果它真的重要，它会重新浮到我的笔记最上面。

sentences.en: And I used to worry about that, but now I'm just like, oh, whatever, yeah, it'll come back.
sentences.zh: 我以前会焦虑这个，但现在我就是：哦，随便吧，它自己会回来的。

sentences.en: We're in a different state now where that idea doesn't matter anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经进入了一个新的状态，那个想法已经不重要了。

sentences.en: So I want you to practice not writing something down for now.
sentences.zh: 所以我想让你练习一下，暂时不把东西写下来。

sentences.en: I'm not saying that's a worthless activity, but just stay in the stream of consciousness for the seven day protocol.
sentences.zh: 我不是说记笔记没用，但在这七天的实验里，就让自己待在意识流里。

sentences.en: Don't reach for your own phone, and just learn to trust your own mind.
sentences.zh: 别去拿手机，学着信任你自己的大脑。

sentences.en: Now, the second thing is to have one real conversation.
sentences.zh: 第二件事，进行一次真正的对话。

sentences.en: No catching up for five minutes before your next meeting.
sentences.zh: 不是在下一个会议前花五分钟寒暄一下近况。

sentences.en: No networking to form a business connection that feels fake.
sentences.zh: 不是为了建立商业关系而去社交，那种感觉很假。

sentences.en: We're not trying to perform here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里不是要表演。

sentences.en: We're trying to remove the performative act.
sentences.zh: 我们要把表演的成分去掉。

sentences.en: So you want to listen to other people's perspectives and attempt to be as present as possible, and your brain may just light up.
sentences.zh: 你要去听别人的视角，尽可能保持临在，你的大脑可能就会亮起来。

sentences.en: And the last thing, extend the walk and you might find that you don't want to stop now.
sentences.zh: 最后一件事，把散步时间延长，你可能会发现自己现在不想停下来了。

sentences.en: Day seven is to finally create with what emerged.
sentences.zh: 第七天，终于要用涌现出来的东西去创造了。

sentences.en: You're going to create something.
sentences.zh: 你要创造点什么。

sentences.en: And this is actually going to be a part of the next video, which is why writing an essay is such a powerful practice, why it's something that you should probably do because an essay doesn't start with a conclusion.
sentences.zh: 这其实会是下一支视频的一部分，也就是为什么写一篇文章是如此强大的练习，为什么你很可能应该去做这件事，因为一篇文章不是从一个结论开始的。

sentences.en: You figure out the conclusion as you write.
sentences.zh: 你是在写的过程中才搞明白结论的。

sentences.en: It's a way of figuring out what you think about things in article.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在写作中理清自己对事物的看法的方式。

sentences.en: On the other hand, for the sake of giving distinction, while these things can overlap in many ways, it starts with the topic. It starts with the conclusion.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，为了做个区分——虽然这些东西在很多方面可以重叠——文章是从主题开始的，是从结论开始的。

sentences.en: You map out the structure and you like fill it in.
sentences.zh: 你搭好结构，然后往里填内容。

sentences.en: And it's like informative in a sense.
sentences.zh: 它在某种意义上更像是信息性的。

sentences.en: And now why we waited for seven days to actually create something is because most people try to create from a depleted state, either a depleted state or just a overstimulated state.
sentences.zh: 而我们为什么等了七天才真正去创造，是因为大多数人试图从一个枯竭的状态去创造，要么是枯竭，要么就是过度刺激的状态。

sentences.en: And then everything just feels forced.
sentences.zh: 然后一切都感觉很勉强。

sentences.en: And I know this feeling well because I've written a newsletter, I've written articles, I've created content for the past five years, consistently long form content.
sentences.zh: 我对这种感觉太熟悉了，因为我写 newsletter、写文章、创作内容已经五年了，持续地产出长内容。

sentences.en: I've done short form for longer than that.
sentences.zh: 我做短内容的时间比这还长。

sentences.en: But this last month, like I talked about, it just felt forced.
sentences.zh: 但过去这一个月，就像我说的，一切都感觉很勉强。

sentences.en: I didn't have anything to write about because I was in this overstimulated state, and I've had many times throughout my career, so to say, where I felt depleted, where I haven't had anything to write.
sentences.zh: 我没什么可写的，因为我处在这种过度刺激的状态里，而且在我所谓的职业生涯里，有很多次我都感到枯竭，什么都写不出来。

sentences.en: But I tried to force it out anyways because I wasn't in this creative way of living.
sentences.zh: 但我还是硬挤，因为我没有活在这种创造性的生活方式里。

sentences.en: So now that we've spent six days creating space, processing information, and letting connections form, we can actually create from a place of abundance now.
sentences.zh: 所以，既然我们已经花了六天来创造空间、处理信息、让连接自然形成，现在我们可以真正从一个丰盈的状态去创造了。

sentences.en: So two things here.
sentences.zh: 这里有两件事。

sentences.en: First, make something with no plan.
sentences.zh: 第一，不带任何计划去做点什么。

sentences.en: Write, draw, record a 20 minute voice note, or cook without a recipe.
sentences.zh: 去写、去画、录一段20分钟的语音笔记，或者不看菜谱做顿饭。

sentences.en: The only rule is no rules, no strategic thinking or trying to find the perfect angle here.
sentences.zh: 唯一的规则就是没有规则，不要做任何战略思考，也别试图找到那个完美的角度。

sentences.en: Just start a thread and follow it.
sentences.zh: 就从一个念头开始，顺着它往下走。

sentences.en: Now the second thing is don't share it.
sentences.zh: 第二件事是，别分享它。

sentences.en: I know this is antithetical to everything that I preach, but we need to remember what it's like to not have silent opinions influencing your direction.
sentences.zh: 我知道这跟我平时倡导的一切完全相反，但我们需要重新记起，不被那些无声的意见影响方向是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Notice how it feels to have made something that's yours.
sentences.zh: 去体会那种做出完全属于你自己的东西的感觉。

sentences.en: And then after at least 24 hours, then you have my permission.
sentences.zh: 然后，至少等24小时之后，你才得到我的许可。

sentences.en: Not that you need my permission to share it, post it somewhere, be my guest.
sentences.zh: 不是说你需要我的许可才能分享，把它发到某个地方，请便。

sentences.en: And if you enjoy that practice and you don't know what to post or share or how to do it, then again, I'd recommend joining the writing or content challenge that starts very soon.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这个练习，但不知道该发什么、分享什么或者怎么做，那我再次推荐你加入那个很快就要开始的写作或内容挑战。

sentences.en: Link in the description for that, but it's to build a two hour content system in 14 days with 14 AI prompts to help you do that faster and more creatively, and not just have it write everything for you.
sentences.zh: 链接在简介里，但它的目标是在14天内，用14个AI提示词帮你建立一个两小时内容系统，让你做得更快、更有创意，而不是让AI替你写完所有东西。

sentences.en: Now, what we're doing on that seventh day is we're separating generative thinking from evaluative thinking.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们在第七天要做的是，把生成性思维和评估性思维分开。

sentences.en: So normally this happens in tandem, like when you're writing an article or a newsletter intentionally, you're trying to produce novel ideas and like, criticize them and edit them at the same time.
sentences.zh: 通常这两者是同步进行的，比如当你有意识地写一篇文章或一期newsletter时，你一边试图产出新颖的想法，一边又在同时批评和编辑它们。

sentences.en: But when you do that, you suppress the generative thinking's potential.
sentences.zh: 但当你这样做时，你就压制了生成性思维的潜力。

sentences.en: The level of novel and creative ideas you can have is kind of suppressed by the part of your mind that is critiquing them and judging them and telling you that they're worthless.
sentences.zh: 你所能拥有的新颖和创造性想法的水平，某种程度上被大脑中那个批判它们、评判它们、告诉你它们毫无价值的部分给压制了。

sentences.en: Now, the last point here, point number four, is that to be creative, you need something to create.
sentences.zh: 现在，最后一点，第四点，要变得有创造力，你需要有东西去创造。

sentences.en: So if we go way back in our lives, maybe I don't know how old you are, but do you remember spelling tests in school?
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们回溯到很久以前的生活，我不知道你多大，但你还记得学校里的拼写测试吗？

sentences.en: Because I remember this vividly, actually, is when I would take a spelling test or prepare for one.
sentences.zh: 因为我对这个记忆犹新，真的，就是当我参加拼写测试或者准备拼写测试的时候。

sentences.en: I don't remember exactly which.
sentences.zh: 我记不清具体是哪个了。

sentences.en: I would learn a new word, and once I learned the new word, I would just start hearing it everywhere like someone would say it.
sentences.zh: 我会学到一个新词，一旦我学会了这个新词，我就开始到处听到它，好像有人会说出来。

sentences.en: As I'm passing them, I would overhear it in conversation.
sentences.zh: 当我路过别人时，我会在对话中无意听到它。

sentences.en: I would see it somewhere written.
sentences.zh: 我会在某个地方看到它被写下来。

sentences.en: I would see it on my computer when I played video games.
sentences.zh: 我会在我打游戏时的电脑上看到它。

sentences.en: And the same thing happens when I saw a new car.
sentences.zh: 同样的事情也发生在我看到一辆新车的时候。

sentences.en: I'm like, oh, that, that's a pretty nice car.
sentences.zh: 我心想，哦，那辆车挺好看的。

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么车？

sentences.en: And then I look it up and then I literally see the next day.
sentences.zh: 然后我去查了一下，结果第二天我真的就看到了。

sentences.en: I just see it everywhere. Let's see like ten of them.
sentences.zh: 我到处都能看到它，好像一下子看到十辆。

sentences.en: And when I started a business or just made it a goal, an actual prioritized goal to start a business, then I would notice more business opportunities.
sentences.zh: 而当我开始创业，或者只是把创业定为一个目标，一个真正优先考虑的目标时，我就会注意到更多的商业机会。

sentences.en: And I didn't know these existed before, because I was made to believe that getting a 9 to 5 job was like my only option.
sentences.zh: 我以前根本不知道这些机会存在，因为我被灌输的观念是，找一份朝九晚五的工作是我唯一的选择。

sentences.en: So this thing, this phenomenon, is the single most important catalyst for creativity.
sentences.zh: 所以这个东西，这种现象，是创造力的唯一最重要催化剂。

sentences.en: It's the reticular activating system in our brains.
sentences.zh: 它是我们大脑中的网状激活系统。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a homing mechanism, right?
sentences.zh: 它有点像一种自动导航机制，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like a heat seeking missile going towards the heat.
sentences.zh: 就像一枚热追踪导弹，直奔热源而去。

sentences.en: And it's based on what's important to you.
sentences.zh: 而它的依据，就是对你来说重要的事。

sentences.en: It's based on the goals, the unconscious and conscious goals that kind of occupy the frame in your mind.
sentences.zh: 依据的是那些占据你心智框架的目标，无论是有意识的还是无意识的。

sentences.en: So if you're going on the default path your entire life, then you're really only going to notice things that help support you going down the default path.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你一辈子都走在默认路径上，那你只会注意到那些支持你继续走默认路径的东西。

sentences.en: But if you change direction, you truly change direction.
sentences.zh: 但如果你改变方向，真正地改变方向——

sentences.en: And it's not as simple as just saying, oh, I'm going to change direction.
sentences.zh: 这可不是嘴上说一句“哦，我要改变方向”那么简单。

sentences.en: Then you start to notice things that aid in you going that direction.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会开始注意到那些能帮你走向新方向的东西。

sentences.en: Talked about this many times.
sentences.zh: 这个我讲过很多次了。

sentences.en: Go and look at the most popular videos on my channel.
sentences.zh: 去看看我频道里最火的那些视频。

sentences.en: People really resonate with that fact.
sentences.zh: 人们对这一点非常有共鸣。

sentences.en: Go watch any of my videos that have changed your life in the title and it will go for that.
sentences.zh: 去看我那些标题里带“改变你人生”的视频，讲的都是这个。

sentences.en: So you need a meaningful project to work on.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要一个有意义的项目去做。

sentences.en: You need a problem to solve.
sentences.zh: 你需要一个需要解决的问题。

sentences.en: You need a business to build.
sentences.zh: 你需要一个需要构建的事业。

sentences.en: You need to create an essay, a design, whatever you're creating a lens by which you reprogram your mind.
sentences.zh: 你需要去创作一篇文章、一个设计，无论你创造什么，它都是一个透镜，你通过它来重新编程自己的大脑。

sentences.en: Because if you are the culmination of the ideas you've accepted into your head, and the ideas you accept are based on what you deem important, and the only things that were important to you were the school, job and retirement that industrial culture permeated into your parents, teachers, and peers.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你只是你所接受的那些观念的集合体，而你接受什么观念又取决于你认为什么重要，而你过去认为唯一重要的就是上学、工作、退休——这套工业文化渗透进了你父母、老师和同龄人的脑子里。

sentences.en: Then, the primary way to pursue a rare life is to simply question and choose what is important to you.
sentences.zh: 那么，追求一种稀有人生的首要方式，就是去质疑并主动选择什么对你来说是重要的。

sentences.en: When you have something important like a project, a design, a product, even a conversation you overhear on the street becomes creative fuel.
sentences.zh: 当你有了一个重要的事，比如一个项目、一个设计、一个产品，就连你在街上无意听到的一段对话，都会变成创作燃料。

sentences.en: You read a book and the sentence pops out to you, but when another person reads it, they don't get the same effect.
sentences.zh: 你读一本书，某句话会跳出来击中你，但另一个人读同一句话，却不会有同样的感觉。

sentences.en: So without a project, it's like your mind is a boat just drifting in water.
sentences.zh: 所以没有项目的时候，你的大脑就像一艘船，在水上漫无目的地漂着。

sentences.en: The seven day protocol we just did helped calm the storm that was previously there rocking your boat.
sentences.zh: 我们刚做完的七天计划，帮你平息了之前摇晃你小船的风暴。

sentences.en: But even if the sea is calm now and you don't have a direction, you're just a boat floating.
sentences.zh: 但就算现在海面平静了，如果你没有方向，你依然只是一艘漂着的船。

sentences.en: You're just going to stay there.
sentences.zh: 你就只会停在原地。

sentences.en: It's nice, but at some point you're probably going to want to do something.
sentences.zh: 这很舒服，但到了某个节点，你大概还是会想做点什么。

sentences.en: So the question now is what makes a good frame?
sentences.zh: 所以现在的问题是：什么才算一个好的心智框架？

sentences.en: What makes a project worth creating?
sentences.zh: 什么才算一个值得创造的项目？

sentences.en: The first thing is that it has to be something unsolved for you.
sentences.zh: 第一，它必须是一个对你来说尚未解决的问题。

sentences.en: It doesn't have to be completely original or novel, but it must be a challenge.
sentences.zh: 它不需要是完全原创或前所未有的，但它必须是一个挑战。

sentences.en: There must be something you don't know the answer to yet, which allows your subconscious to become a magnet for relevant and useful ideas.
sentences.zh: 必须有一些你还不知道答案的东西，这才能让你的潜意识变成一块磁铁，去吸引相关且有用的想法。

sentences.en: Second, it has to matter to you.
sentences.zh: 第二，它必须对你真正重要。

sentences.en: Your pattern recognition is powered by emotional investment.
sentences.zh: 你的模式识别能力是由情感投入驱动的。

sentences.en: So a project you chose because it looks good on paper, like a high paying degree that you don't actually care about, won't activate the same radar as the one that genuinely keeps you up at night.
sentences.zh: 所以一个你只是因为它“看起来不错”而选的项目，比如一个高薪但你根本不感兴趣的学位，它无法激活那种雷达，只有那个真正让你彻夜难眠的事才能。

sentences.en: And third, it has to be shareable.
sentences.zh: 第三，它必须是可分享的。

sentences.en: In other words, it has to take some form.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它必须有一个形态。

sentences.en: It has to exist.
sentences.zh: 它必须存在。

sentences.en: In reality, it can be words, visuals, code, a conversation, a business or meal.
sentences.zh: 在现实中，它可以是文字、视觉、代码、一段对话、一个生意或一顿饭。

sentences.en: You have to take the abstract thoughts in your head, ground them in reality, and test their worth.
sentences.zh: 你必须把脑子里那些抽象的想法，落地到现实中，检验它们的价值。

sentences.en: We aren't just imagining things we can't do here, and we are.
sentences.zh: 我们不是只在想象那些做不到的事，我们确实在想象。

sentences.en: We're letting our mind get very creative and be like a kid again who wants to build a teleportation device.
sentences.zh: 我们是在让大脑彻底放飞创意，像小孩一样，想造一台瞬间传送装置。

sentences.en: But that's for thinking, right?
sentences.zh: 但那是思考阶段，对吧？

sentences.en: That's for getting the ideas when you actually put them in reality and test them, then yeah, it has to be useful.
sentences.zh: 那是为了获取想法，当你真正把它们放进现实去检验的时候，对，它必须有用。

sentences.en: But don't let that stunt how creative you can think.
sentences.zh: 但别让这一点扼杀你思考的创造力。

sentences.en: And so that begs the final question how do you find this meaningful project that you want to build?
sentences.zh: 这就引出了最后一个问题：你怎么找到那个你想构建的有意义的项目？

sentences.en: And honestly, it just takes a bit of floundering, which is very unpleasant, but it does help.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这需要一点挣扎，过程很不舒服，但确实有用。

sentences.en: If you flip the problem on its head, you invert it.
sentences.zh: 如果你把问题翻转过来，倒过来想。

sentences.en: So what you do is you think deeply about all of the meaningless projects, tasks and activities you currently tolerate to fill your time.
sentences.zh: 你要做的是，深度思考你目前在忍受的所有无意义的项目、任务和活动，那些你用来填满时间的东西。

sentences.en: Because if you aren't engaged in something meaningful, where do you think your life will end up?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你没有投入一件有意义的事，你觉得你的人生最终会走向哪里？

sentences.en: If you cultivate this deep awareness of what you don't want in life that starts to create your frame, you start to see it everywhere, and once you see it, it's much easier to start moving in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 如果你培养出这种对“你不想要什么”的深刻觉察，它就会开始构建你的框架，你会在各处看到它，一旦你看到了，朝反方向走就容易多了。

sentences.en: Thank you for watching.
sentences.zh: 感谢观看。

sentences.en: Like subscribe while you're here if the video actually impacted you.
sentences.zh: 如果这个视频真的触动到你，请点赞、订阅。

sentences.en: Links in the description for my newsletter that I send out weekly with very similar thoughts to this.
sentences.zh: 简介里有我每周发送的 newsletter 链接，内容跟这些思考非常相似。

sentences.en: So if you like this, it's definitely worth reading as well.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这个视频，那篇也绝对值得一读。

sentences.en: So subscribe to that and then just keep an eye out for the next video on why writing essays is very important, and why you should probably do it.
sentences.zh: 所以订阅那个，然后留意下一个视频，讲的是为什么写文章非常重要，以及你为什么可能应该去做这件事。

sentences.en: Thank you again for watching.
sentences.zh: 再次感谢观看。

sentences.en: I'll see you in the next one. Bye.
sentences.zh: 下个视频见。拜。
